track_source: static comparison of built images; no board involved
why: the phase is a RELATIVE timing - which sample of a 512-sample fold is displaced - so it is set when the DAC timer and the ADC trigger are armed, not by what runs afterwards. Seven mechanisms were refuted before anyone looked at the start path.
narrowing: 37 start/arm/init/trigger functions are present in both 8e300d2 and f519890. FIFTEEN differ, and every one of the fifteen differs ONLY in address - the code is identical in all of them. And acq_start and gen_start are identical in code AND address between those two images (0008236c, 00082904) while the phase differs by 21. So between the two, the whole difference in the start path is WHERE stream_core_start and its siblings sit in flash.
hypothesis_tested: address-dependent instruction fetch - the SAM3X flash controller has wait states and a 128-bit read buffer, so identical code at a different alignment can take a different number of cycles, changing the gap between arming the DAC timer and arming the ADC trigger
verdict: NOT SUPPORTED in its simple form
why_refuted: stream_core_start mod 16 is 8 for efa47f8 (phase 135), 398ac94 (phase 5) and 4dc944a (phase 156) - three different phases at one alignment. And 4dc944a and 8e300d2 share phase 156 with entirely different addresses. No naive alignment model predicts the phase across five images.
status: a narrowing, not a mechanism. Eight hypotheses tested tonight and eight refuted; this one is recorded because the NARROWING is solid even though the model is not.
proposed_next: change EEFC FMR FWS at runtime and re-measure. Flash wait states are a register, so fetch timing can be varied on ONE image with no rebuild - which is the discriminating experiment this issue has never had: every arm so far compares images that differ in many ways at once.
